text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- A survey on equality of the sexes in Norwegian companies commissioned by several government ministries shows that efforts to recruit more women in top positions haven't had any effects. The problem is not primarily that women are hampered by maternity leave or small children in their career, but that company boards are old-fashioned in selecting top leaders, who usually are men.
- State-owned oil company Statoil wants to recruit more women, especially in leading positions. By the year 2000 the company will have 20 percent women on all levels of staff.
- The Postal Authority will shut down 1,400 post offices before 1999, saving 800 million crowns a year on the cutbacks.

- Pharmaceutical group Nycomed ASA is looking for ways to save money after booking poor results in the first six months of 1996. Svein Aaser, head of Nycomed, says staff layoffs are planned, but gave no figures.
- Shipowner John Fredriksen is in negotiations with Hyundai in South Korea on building up to four new Suexmax tankers.
